Broken elbow? Shit, that sounds painful. Recover soon.

The injury was full of irony. First, it happened when I slipped on ice...in the parking lot of the gym I go to. I went in anyways, and did cardio on a recumbent bike for about half an hour. (There are shitloads of things that happen during exercise that help with both pain management and injury healing.) The funny thing is, I had no perceivable indications of a fracture: no swelling, no impingement of my elbow's movement, no pain at the site of the fracture and no sensation of bone moving against bone. What hurt like hell was the brachioradiatus, the muscle on the top of the forearm that plays a big role in how you twist your wrist. That got strained by the way I cantilevered my arm when I landed on the elbow, and it hurt like fucking hell. It wasn't until 2 months later, after I whacked my elbow in the shower, that I decided to see a doctor and find what I could do to accelerate my recovery (which had been doing pretty well). They took some x-rays...lo and behold, I'd broken the radial head.

At this point, I'm close to recovered, but the challenge is getting back full range of motion. I kept working out pretty much the whole time...a break of one and a half weeks immediately following the injury, and another break of a week once I was told by the doctor that I had sustained a fracture and should stop loading the arm until I saw the ortho. The good news of that is that I didn't lose nearly as much strength in the arm as I would have otherwise. The bad news is that it did contribute a bit to losing some extension, but I'm 10 degrees away from being back to normal there now anyways.

Go figure...I do all kinds of dangerous activities, but I break my elbow while walking across a parking lot. I never get hurt doing risky stuff...
